To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

the prevalence of surrogate alcohol use among Russian population is relatively low, but the consumption of surrogate alcohols is associated with the increased risk of death due to alcohol-related causes.

(1) the prevalence of noncommercial alcohol consumption among the general population of Russia is relatively high; (2) the consumption of noncommercial alcohol is associated with a high level of alcohol use disorders; and (3) there is an urgent need for further research to better characterize noncommercial alcohol consumption, its health effects, and the factors associated with this behavior.
the consumption of nonbeverage and surrogate alcohol is a serious public health problem in the Russian Federation and that it is associated with the risk of alcohol dependence.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the development and testing of a new approach to solving problems of alcohol consumption.
the development and implementation of the system for the analysis of the state of the alcohol market and the dynamics of the alcohol consumption in Russia.
the problem of the formation of the Russian alcohol culture in the context of globalization.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
nonbeverage alcohol consumption is an important problem that needs to be addressed in Russia.
nonbeverage alcohol consumption in the former Soviet Union, and in Russia in particular, is not a rare phenomenon, it is widespread and has been increasing.
the problem of nonbeverage alcohol consumption in Russia is a serious problem and requires further study.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the Russian alcohol market is a unique one.
the Russian government should develop and implement policies to reduce nonbeverage alcohol consumption and its consequences.
the Russian alcohol market is characterized by a large shadow segment, and the consumption of surrogate alcohol is a widespread phenomenon in the country.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the consumption of surrogate alcohol is a serious public health issue.
, despite the high prevalence of alcohol use, the majority of Russians are not heavy drinkers.

the prevalence of surrogate alcohol consumption is higher among the population with a low socioeconomic status, and the consumption of surrogate alcohol is associated with a higher prevalence of alcohol use disorders and a lower likelihood of seeking help for alcohol-related problems.
